prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
UKIP’s 2010 manifesto centres on leaving the European Union to restore UK sovereignty, reclaim legislative control, and redirect money and policy across all areas of government. It argues EU membership imposes heavy costs, regulation and legal constraints, and that a UK outside the EU could keep free trade while regaining control over borders, laws and budgets.

Core economic and fiscal policies
- Tax and spending: Raise the personal allowance to £11,500; introduce a single 31% flat tax (merging income tax and employee NI), take more low earners out of tax; phase out Employers’ NI over five years; aim to reduce the public sector to roughly its 1997 size; cut quangos and “non-jobs”; abolish Inheritance Tax when affordable; replace VAT with a Local Sales Tax sharing revenue with councils.
- Regulation and banking: Scrap large volumes of EU-derived rules; return financial oversight to the Bank of England; raise bank capital requirements; separate retail and investment banking (Glass-Steagall style); reinstate a lending “corset.”

Jobs, enterprise and skills
- Industrial strategy: Create around 1m skilled jobs via long-term programmes in defence procurement, nuclear power build-out, flood/coastal defences, transport infrastructure, and prison construction, with priority for British-based firms.
- Business support and skills: Establish Production Enterprise Centres; denationalise universities/FE with student/training vouchers; curb hostile EU measures (e.g., carbon schemes) and protect strategic firms from foreign takeovers.

Immigration and asylum
- Impose a five-year freeze on immigration for permanent settlement; afterward, a tightly controlled points-based system (c. 50,000 p.a.); leave the EU to regain border control; tripled border staff; no amnesty for illegal immigrants; secure processing of asylum claims; repeal the Human Rights Act and withdraw from the ECHR; restore the Primary Purpose Rule; end state promotion of multiculturalism.

Law and order
- Elected county police boards; “life means life”; double prison places; three-strikes policy; stronger homeowner protection; withdraw from the European Arrest Warrant; youth “boot camps”; abolish the Crown Prosecution Service.

Defence and foreign policy
- Increase defence spending by ~40%; expand the Army and TA; rebuild the Navy (including three new carriers); more RAF lift/rotary and JSF aircraft; maintain and replace the nuclear deterrent; prioritise NATO; reassess Afghanistan.
- Leave the EU political union; pursue Swiss-style FTA; reclaim a direct WTO seat; champion a Commonwealth Free Trade Area; support global democracy/human rights.

Public services and welfare
- NHS: No frontline cuts; elected county health boards; reduce bureaucracy (abolish SHAs/PCTs); franchise services on fixed budgets; health vouchers to opt out; restore matrons; free eye tests and dental checks.
- Education: School vouchers; retain and expand grammar/specialist (“professional”) schools; less central prescription; elected county education boards; franchise provision; restore grants via student vouchers; reduce university target.
- Pensions and welfare: A non-means-tested Citizen’s Pension of at least £130/week at 65; reinstate dividend tax credit; freeze unaffordable public sector schemes; simplify benefits into a Basic Cash Benefit; enhanced child and nursery vouchers; workfare; restrict benefits to citizens or 5-year residents.

Energy, environment and infrastructure
- Climate-sceptic stance; target up to 50% electricity from nuclear; support domestic coal; oppose most onshore wind; repeal the Climate Change Act and restrictive EU directives; invest an extra £3bn p.a. in transport; new high-speed rail lines; Thames Estuary airport; Britdisc for foreign lorries.

Governance, housing and culture
- Direct democracy with citizen-initiated referenda; mixed-member electoral reform (AV+); elected county boards (police, health, education); abolish regional government; recall MPs; support monarchy/Church; English Parliament arrangements.
- Planning led by local referenda; protect green belt; scrap regional strategies and HIPs; incentivise empty home use; enable more social housing.
- Civic nationalism; oppose multiculturalism; protect British brands/measures; ban burqa/niqab in specified settings; deport radical preachers; celebrate Commonwealth and English identities.

Rural, fishing and other policies
- Agriculture: Leave CAP gradually, promote British produce, GM research with labelling, strengthen producer co-ops and supermarket regulation.
- Fisheries: Leave CFP; 200-mile EEZ; end discards; no-take zones; ban industrial trawling; boost enforcement.
- Support Royal Mail/Post Offices; allow smoking rooms in pubs; champion small businesses and animal welfare.
